Canaan is a well done single-season anime. There's also a video game "prequel" of it. The protagonist has a mutated form of synesthesia which makes for a really unique action/adventure story.

One Punch Man explores the troubles of being the "strongest" hero.

Case Closed (or Detective Conan) is what got me hooked. It's realistic enough, save for a little suspension of disbelief. Followed closely is Spiral, which is another (single season) detective-esque story that I thoroughly enjoyed.

And most recently, Attack on Titan has a story that absolutely pulled me in. From the same director of Death Note, a "classic" as far as anime goes.

A lot of anime stories are reality-based enough to be more enjoyable for me. Like Sword Art Online. The story is alright, but even as a sci-fi work, it's plausible enough to draw me in.

All in all, it's a fairly enjoyable genre. Oftentimes better entertainment than whatever Hollywood spews out.
